note: Adapted from the species description of Sands (1972); the original is in English and the genus has no soldier caste, only the alate and worker being described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Both castes are distinguished from the closely related A. amicus, A. concilians and A. eumenus by the broad base of the second marginal tooth of the right mandible and the smaller first marginal tooth. The differences from A. benignus are given under that species. The reduction of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible in the worker may also indicate a trend towards the species of Group III; but, as the compound ratios show, the mandibular proportions are in fact different, and the junction of the mesenteron and proctodaeum is also shorter. A further character is that the abdomen of the worker of A. comis appears not to dehisce.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white, pilosity concolorous, extremely sparse, fine and short. Postclypeus strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.32–0.35, Pcl/Ri 3.04–3.95. Apical tooth of mandibles rather short, La/Li 0.56–0.61, Ra/Ri 0.69–0.80; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just separated from the molar prominence in surface view, compound ratio 14.8–18.6; tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly posterior to the line from the apical to the second marginal tooth, its anterior edge distinctly shorter than that of the second marginal tooth, which has a broad base, compound ratio 18.29–22.15. Fore tibia moderately inflated, Ti/Tw 3.90–4.07, third apical spur conspicuous. Junction of mesenteron and proctodaeum almost transverse, coincident with the Malpighian nodule; enteric valve seating lateral in the undissected abdomen, very weakly bilobed, almost a mere rim, sessile and attached to the second proctodaeal pouch; membranous wall of the valve with sparse spinules outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule sepia brown, deep sepia brown above the ocelli, the dark area usually extending as tapering stripes converging on the fontanelle; fontanelle small, oval, flat, indistinct, concolorous with the head; mid-spot elongate-oval, about as large as the fontanelle, also concolorous with the head; postclypeus brown, labrum pale brown; frontal mark a weak, flat crescent, brown; antennae pale brown. Pronotum brown, meso- and metanotum pale brown, the transverse dark suture weak on the mesonotum and distinct on the metanotum; femora and tibiae pale brown, tarsi yellowish white. Abdominal tergites and the sides of the sternites pale brown, the middle of the sternites yellowish white, spiracles sclerotised; cerci yellowish white. Posterior margin of head capsule rather unevenly rounded, slightly undulate; ocelli medium-sized, separated from the compound eye by two-fifths to three-quarters of their minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.27–0.31, Pcl/Ra 3.21–4.15, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Apical tooth of mandibles short, La/Li 0.51–0.63, Ra/Rj 0.65–0.82; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just separated from the molar prominence in surface view, compound ratio 8.66–10.91; tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly posterior to the line from the apical to the second marginal tooth, its anterior edge slightly shorter than that of the second marginal tooth, which has a broad base. Pilosity of head capsule brown, dense, uneven, not felted. Third apical spur of fore tibia well developed.
